Question: What is the difference between the sequential and recurrent generation schemes?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 1, page 3) (image attached): Figure 1: Illustration of different condition video generation schemes. (a) Frame-to-frame generation scheme (no correlation across different frames). (b) Sequential frame generation scheme (only short term frame correlation is considered). The dash block in- dicates when L = 2 . (c) Recurrent frame generation scheme where the identity image I ∗ is fed into all the future frame generation to preserve long-term dependency.
Words printed in the figure: (a) Frame (b) Sequential (c) Recurrent
[E2] (figure, Figure 1, page 3): a zoomed view of Figure 1 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: The sequential frame generation scheme considers only short term frame correlation.

cites.quote: (b) Sequential frame generation scheme (only short term frame correlation is considered).

claims.text: In the recurrent frame generation scheme, the identity image is fed into all future frame generations to preserve long-term dependency.

cites.quote: (c) Recurrent frame generation scheme where the identity image I ∗ is fed into all the future frame generation to preserve long-term dependency.
